In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the disulfide is not a mere folding catalyst but a structural element that contributes to the stability of the native state, as well as to the folding rate, and that its presence can change the folding mechanism.
the disulfide is not an obligatory factor for the fast folding rate, but it is a major determinant, and it can accelerate the folding process by a factor of 100-1000.
the presence of disulfide bonds in proteins may have an important influence on their folding kinetics and that the disulfide bonds are a determinant of the folding rates in proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the folding process of AcP from E. coli is remarkably accelerated in the presence of the disulfide.

the presence of the disulfide in the wild-type EcoAcP allows the folding to proceed via a two-state mechanism with a very fast folding rate, and the disulfide also allows the wild-type protein to fold more quickly than the mutEcoAcp.
the presence of the disulfide in EcoAcP accelerates its folding rate by a factor of ca 1500.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of the disulfide stabilizes the folding intermediate of the protein, thus allowing it to reach the native state more quickly.
the presence of the disulfide in EcoAcP accelerates folding by a factor of 1500, as compared with mut E. coli AcP, which folds according to a standard nucleation-condensation mechanism.
the folding of a disulfides containing protein may be faster or slower than that of its mutant lacking the disulfides.
